opal:
Stood a house for a royal bride,
Built all of changing opal stone,
The royal palace, till now descried

And made it less substantial. And I knew
The harmless opal snakes, and large-mouthed frogs,
(Those noisy vaunters of their shallow streams)

See how the speckled sky burns like a pigeon's throat,
Jewelled with embers of opal and peridote.

A jewel that grew dull in garish light,
An opal which beneath my wondering gaze
Gleamed rarely, softly throbbing in the night.
opaque: There was something beyond the tree—a whiteness, a softness, an opaque mass, half-hidden—with delicate pillars.

His crest was amber glittered with blue,
And opaque so the sun came shining through.
It seemed a crown with fiery points.
Driven of the spirit, long have I sought to temper it unto the spirit’s longing, But my mind, too, is opaque to the soul.
The eldest boy, Esau, had been a journeyman tailor for ten years; the girl next him, Ora, was plump, dark, freckled; others came--a string of ulcered girls until finally a pretty, opaque one, Maura.
His writing is opaque rather than transparent; we see no depths through it, nor any very secret movements of mind or heart.

opals: She had a large and beautiful angora cat, it used to sit in the tray of amethysts and opals and stare at her from very bright cold eyes.
Opals and emeralds, they lie about the roots of turnips.
